headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, revenue trends are mixed while cost‑cutting and AI initiatives dominate.
summary: Media firms show solid top‑line growth but are tightening IT spend to fund restructuring. Gaming operators are split, with Bally's expanding revenue while Caesars posts a loss and tightens budgets. Publishing sees divergent performance; Pearson accelerates while Scholastic misses targets. Education entities range from Pearson’s growth to SLU’s service outsourcing and staff cuts.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and a 43% jump in operating income. WBD/Skydance and Versant also delivered positive results. Cost‑cutting and AI projects are prominent.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: Disney targets $3 bn savings by 2029; WBD plans $6 bn annual cuts.

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney explores AI in parks; Versant expands streaming platforms.

themes.title: Digital rebuild
themes.detail: Versant added FAST channels and new streaming memberships.

industries.it_note: IT budgets are being trimmed to fund large‑scale cost‑saving programs across the sector.

industries.summary: Bally's revenue surged 21.7% while Caesars recorded a $123 m loss. Light & Wonder and Brightstar show stable margins but are tightening spend.

leaders.why: Revenue up 21.7% YoY, strong segment growth

laggards.why: Widened GAAP loss of $123 m in Q3

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
